definition: Clinical and advocacy term for a person born with sex characteristics that do not fit typical binary definitions of male or female.
notes: Direct calque of English 'intersex(ual)'; standard in medical and LGBTQ+ advocacy discourse across all Spanish-speaking regions.

definition: English loanword adopted as an umbrella term for non-heterosexual and non-cisgender identities in Spanish-language LGBTQ+ and academic discourse.
notes: Pronunciation follows English; usage concentrated in urban, educated, and activist circles; more prevalent in Latin America than Spain; does not carry the historical sting of the English slur in Spanish contexts.

definition: A gender identity that does not fall exclusively within the traditional binary categories of man or woman.
notes: Direct calque of English 'non-binary'; adjective agreement varies by speaker — 'no binarie' is used as a gender-neutral form in some activist communities.

definition: A person who experiences sexual attraction only after forming a significant emotional bond with someone.
notes: Direct English loanword; recognition largely confined to online asexuality-spectrum and LGBTQ+ communities; negligible outside those circles.

definition: A gender identity characterized by fluidity, shifting between or among gender expressions rather than remaining fixed at one point on the spectrum.
notes: Direct translation of English 'gender fluid'; also appears as the untranslated loanword 'genderfluid'; primarily activist and academic usage; low recognition among older Spanish speakers.

definition: Highly offensive slur for a gay man; also deployed as a general-purpose insult for any weak, cowardly, or contemptible man regardless of sexuality.
notes: The single most universally recognized gay slur in the Spanish-speaking world; augmentative of 'marica'; used as a standalone expletive, general insult, and targeted homophobic attack; partially reclaimed in some Latin American gay communities.

definition: A slur for an effeminate or gay man; softer than 'maricón' and partially reclaimed as a neutral or affectionate term of address within some Latin American gay communities.
notes: Base form from which 'maricón' and 'mariquita' derive; in Colombia and parts of South America, widely reclaimed as a casual in-group address between gay men with reduced stigma.

definition: Slur for a gay man or male sex worker; also functions as a powerful all-purpose intensifier and insult across Spanish.
notes: Male counterpart of 'puta'; primary meanings oscillate between gay slur and male prostitute depending on region; in Mexico additionally serves as one of the most versatile expletives in the language; meaning highly context-dependent.

definition: Mexican and Central American slur for a gay or effeminate man; one of the primary anti-gay insults in Mexico.
notes: Predominantly Mexican and Central American; rarely used in Spain or South America; etymology disputed — possible link to Tagalog 'hoto' or to the letter J in Spanish; partially reclaimed in Mexican gay culture.

definition: Mexican slur derived from 'culo' (ass), meaning a man who has anal sex; used as a gay slur and as a general insult for a contemptible or cowardly person.
notes: Primarily Mexican Spanish; the gay-slur and general-insult meanings coexist; analogous to how English 'asshole' can be purely insulting without sexual specificity, but in Mexican context the anal-sex implication is active.

definition: Diminutive of 'marica'; a moderately offensive slur for an effeminate or gay man, somewhat gentler than 'maricón' but still pejorative.
notes: Literally 'little Mary' and also the word for ladybug (Coccinella); the doubled meaning lends it a mocking, diminutive quality; often directed at boys and young men; less severe than 'maricón' in most regional registers.

definition: Augmentative of 'marica'; a strong slur for a gay or extremely effeminate man, the intensifying '-ón' suffix amplifying the insult.
notes: The augmentative form implies greater degree than 'marica'; widely used across Spain and Latin America; recognized pan-regionally though more common in Spain and the Southern Cone.

definition: An effeminate man; a man displaying stereotypically feminine mannerisms or behavior; implicitly codes as homosexual in everyday usage though not definitionally so.
notes: Can be purely descriptive or mildly pejorative depending on tone and context; less loaded than the 'mari-' family of slurs; used in both clinical descriptions and casual conversation; does not inherently name sexuality.

definition: Archaic term for a homosexual person derived from 19th-century sexology's theory of 'sexual inversion' as a pathological reversal of normal gender roles and desires.
notes: Borrowed directly from Krafft-Ebing and Havelock Ellis's 'sexual inversion' framework; appeared in Spanish legal, medical, and literary texts through the mid-20th century; now obsolete except in historical quotation.

definition: Religious and legal term for a person who practices sodomy; historically used primarily to condemn and prosecute gay men; derived from the biblical city of Sodom.
notes: Maintained in conservative Catholic and evangelical discourse; was an operative legal category in Spanish colonial and Inquisitorial law; peak usage spans the colonial period; still deployed in some religious contexts today.

definition: Offensive slur for a lesbian woman; literally 'female tortilla maker,' a metaphor invoking the grinding and rubbing motion of tribadism.
notes: Widely used throughout Spain and recognized across Latin America; the culinary metaphor (tortilla-pressing as genital rubbing) is transparent to most speakers; partially reclaimed by Spanish lesbian activists and communities.

definition: A masculine-presenting or tomboy woman; a slur implying that a woman is excessively masculine, often carrying implied lesbianism though not exclusively.
notes: Compound of feminine name 'María' and 'macho' (male/masculine); less severe than 'bollera' or 'tortillera'; sometimes applied to heterosexual tomboys without lesbian implication; partially reclaimed in some queer communities.

definition: Spanish slur for a butch or heavily masculine-presenting lesbian woman; literally 'female truck driver,' invoking the cultural stereotype of truckers as hyper-masculine.
notes: Primarily Castilian Spanish usage; the truck-driver stereotype parallels English 'diesel dyke'; less commonly used in Latin America; targets specifically the masculine-presenting end of lesbian identity presentation.

definition: Highly offensive Castilian Spanish slur for a lesbian woman; one of the two primary anti-lesbian insults in Spain alongside 'tortillera.'
notes: Primarily used in Spain; etymology disputed — possibly from 'bollo' (bun/bread roll) as vulgar slang for vulva; widely reclaimed by Spanish lesbian activists, particularly the organization Las Bollos; analogous in reclamation arc to English 'dyke.'

definition: Offensive Latin American slur for a transgender woman, shortening of 'travestida' or 'travesti.'
notes: Predominantly Argentine and Río de la Plata usage; has undergone significant reclamation within Argentine trans activist communities — the organization ATTTA (Asociación de Travestis, Transexuales y Transgéneros de Argentina) embraces 'travesti' as an identity; 'trava' as shortened form remains contested.

definition: Argentine and Uruguayan slur for a gay or effeminate man; also used loosely as a general insult for a foolish or contemptible person.
notes: Primarily Argentine and Uruguayan; etymology uncertain; partially reclaimed in Buenos Aires gay culture where it can be used as an in-group term with reduced hostility; less widely recognized outside the Southern Cone.

definition: Spanish slur for an effeminate or camp gay man, implying theatrical, flamboyant, or over-the-top feminine behavior.
notes: Primarily Castilian Spanish; etymology disputed — possibly from 'sarasa' (printed cotton chintz fabric, connoting something gaudy and floral) or from a proper name; targets visible campness and gender nonconformity specifically.

definition: Literally 'madwoman'; used across Latin American gay communities for a flamboyant or effeminate gay man; simultaneously a pejorative slur and a widely embraced in-group identity term.
notes: One of the most culturally rich terms in this set; functions on a spectrum from slur to celebration depending on who uses it; central to Latin American camp and drag culture; the word's feminine gender is part of its subversive force.

definition: Literally 'old madwoman'; Latin American slang for an older flamboyant or effeminate gay man; tone ranges from affectionate irreverence to dismissive ageism depending on the speaker's relationship to the target.
notes: Compounds 'vieja' (old woman) with 'loca' (queen/madwoman); the age marker adds a layer absent from 'loca' alone — can signal either fond familiarity toward an elder of the community or dismissal of someone past their sexual prime.

definition: Euphemism for a gay person, literally 'one who understands' or 'someone in the know'; used as a discreet coded signal of homosexual identity, especially during the Franco dictatorship in Spain.
notes: Classic coded euphemism of Franco-era Spain, when open gay identity was criminally dangerous; semantically similar to English 'friend of Dorothy' or 'family'; declining since the Transition but still recognized by older speakers; the feminine 'entendida' was used for lesbians.
